CHIEF COMPLAINT
Breast reduction consultation

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Julia Jones is a 25-year-old female presenting for evaluation of breast reduction. She has been considering this procedure for approximately 6-7 years. She reports symptomatic macromastia with chronic back pain, neck pain, and upper back pain that have been present since high school. Pain builds up throughout the day, particularly when working at a desk. She has been attending a chiropractor for several years with minimal relief. She experiences occasional numbness and tingling in her hands. She reports bra strap indentations on her shoulders and typically wears a 34E sports bra for comfort, as larger regular bras are expensive. She denies rashes underneath her breasts but notes they are always sweaty. She reports significant activity limitations due to breast size, including difficulty with exercise, jumping, and running, which cause pain and require her to hold them for support. She has not had a previous consultation regarding breast reduction. Recently lost 10 pounds and desires to lose an additional 20 pounds.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for back pain, neck pain, upper back pain, occasional hand numbness and tingling, and activity limitations with exercise. Negative for rashes under breasts, breast tenderness, or nipple pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Symptomatic macromastia; Family history of breast cancer (mother at age 40)

MEDICATIONS
Propranolol (for migraines)

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother diagnosed with breast cancer at age 40; Patient advised to begin mammograms at age 30

SOCIAL HISTORY
Currently enrolled in college studying psychology. Occasional alcohol use (wine). Denies tobacco and drug use. Married; husband recently accepted new job. Currently has Blue Cross Blue Shield insurance; will be transitioning to husband's insurance plan (non-Blue Cross) in July. Works at desk.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Inspection reveals asymmetrical breasts with severe bilateral ptosis. One breast positioned slightly lower than the other. No nipple retraction or discharge noted bilaterally. No breast tenderness, masses, or axillary lymphadenopathy palpable. Measurements obtained. Estimated cup size approximately G cup; patient typically wears 34E sports bra.

RESULTS
BSA: 2.65 m². Schnur scale minimum required resection: 1,792 grams. Anticipated final cup size: small C cup. Patient is an excellent candidate for bilateral reduction mammoplasty.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
25-year-old female with symptomatic macromastia presenting for breast reduction evaluation. Discussed bilateral reduction mammoplasty via anchor incision technique with nipple elevation. Explained surgical procedure, anticipated resection of 1,792 grams minimum, expected operative time of 3 hours, bilateral drain placement for approximately 1 week, and one-night hospital stay. Counseled regarding post-operative activity restrictions: no heavy lifting for 6 weeks, no driving for 2-3 weeks. Discussed potential complications including slight risk of altered nipple sensation, approximately 30% risk of inability to breastfeed, breast changes with weight gain or pregnancy, scarring with expected timeline of one year for maturation, and normal post-operative bruising. Explained expected benefits including immediate relief of back and neck pain. Patient counseled to contact office once new insurance information is obtained in July. Plan to submit prior authorization to insurance company and schedule surgery once approval received. Pre-operative visit will be scheduled prior to surgery. Photos to be obtained today for insurance submission.
